statusDetail: The requested host redirects to https://filmyfly.soy/. All 58 catalog checks were judged across the homepage, legal/content template, contact template and intentional 404 recovery state.

page.framework: None detected; server-rendered static HTML with inline CSS and a small inline script.
page.notes: filmyfly.racing redirects to filmyfly.soy. Public sitemap contains five routes. Home is a long entertainment-search landing page; privacy/terms/DMCA/contact share a legal-content template. Terms and DMCA were represented by privacy/contact because their template and navigation pattern are shared.

principleOutcomes.reason: This static informational site exposes no transactional capability for an agent; its public prose is already fully present in raw HTML. The static reading/navigation experience has no inference task for which an on-device model would provide proportionate user value.

paths.description: Entry page and primary entertainment-search journey; highest-risk landing template and all primary calls to action.
Representative long-form legal/content template; covers privacy disclosure, in-page navigation and crawled metadata. Terms and DMCA share this archetype and were not duplicated.
Representative support/contact destination and cross-page navigation template; verifies that contact is mailto-based rather than an authored form.
Intentional missing route to exercise HTTP failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: Non-essential reveal and hover transitions remain enabled when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched prefers-reduced-motion: reduce but found no matching override; each .feature-card retained two 0.5s transitions and the inline IntersectionObserver reveal still applies.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule that removes non-essential transitions and make the reveal immediately visible; follow the accessibility guidance.

findings.summary: Full-page navigations swap abruptly with no cross-document View Transition.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found zero view-transition rules across a multi-page site with home, policy, contact, terms and DMCA routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared header/content where motion is allowed.

findings.summary: Scroll-entry reveals are driven by JavaScript and inline transitions rather than declarative CSS scroll/view timelines.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains an IntersectionObserver that mutates opacity/transform; the platform probe found zero animation-timeline rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer a CSS view() timeline for progressive reveal, with content visible by default and a reduced-motion override.

findings.summary: The primary page buries useful navigation under a very long, repetitive search-keyword document.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout measured 12,653 CSS px tall. The DOM repeats FilmyFly/Filmy4wap and format keywords through many bordered panels while all prominent calls to action point back to the same page.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace duplicated keyword sections with a concise explanation and real category/navigation content; defer genuinely secondary material.

findings.summary: Reusable card components adapt only through intrinsic grids and viewport media queries, not their own container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero @container rules; feature/content/contact cards are reused in responsive grids and their typography/padding only changes at viewport breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare an inline-size container on card grids and move component-specific adaptations into @container queries where card width, not viewport width, is the dependency.

findings.summary: The page promises entertainment search but exposes no search control, category result, or concrete content destination.
findings.evidence: The first viewport presents a search-result facsimile and several calls to action, but DOM inspection found only links and no search input; all movie/category links resolve to the same homepage with tracking query parameters.
findings.suggestedFix: State the actual page purpose plainly and expose one honest primary action that reaches real, distinct content or a functional search.

findings.summary: The representative “explore movies and web series” journey cannot be completed.
findings.evidence: Recon showed “Latest Movies”, “Web Series”, “View Full Site”, “Explore Movies & Web Series”, and “Visit Official Website Now” all target https://filmyfly.soy/ with query parameters; loading them returns the same landing page rather than results or a distinct full site.
findings.suggestedFix: Build real destination routes/search results and verify each primary CTA end-to-end; otherwise remove claims that imply a usable entertainment catalog.

findings.summary: The HTTPS response lacks both Content-Security-Policy and HSTS.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS and nosniff/frame/referrer/permissions protections, but reported Content-Security-Policy: missing and Strict-Transport-Security: missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP compatible with the inline assets (prefer hashes/nonces or externalized CSS/JS), then add HSTS after validating HTTPS coverage.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced XSS and transport defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers provide SAMEORIGIN, nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and a restrictive Permissions-Policy, but no CSP/frame-ancestors policy and no HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors and an HSTS policy; retain the existing permissions, referrer, frame and MIME protections.

findings.summary: Language is declared, but the authored layout is not ready for bidirectional presentation.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found html lang="en-IN" but no dir attribute. CSS repeatedly uses physical properties such as padding-left, margin-left and border-left rather than logical equivalents, despite copy claiming a multilingual audience.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit direction where appropriate and replace physical inline-direction properties with logical properties such as padding-inline-start and border-inline-start.

findings.summary: The page imitates a search result and uses destination labels that do not match the actual navigation.
findings.evidence: The first card visually resembles a search result, displays https://filmyfly.faith while linking to filmyfly.soy, and labels same-page loops as “View Full Site” and “Visit Official Website Now”.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the search-result facsimile and domain mismatch; use accurate link labels and disclose destinations before navigation.

findings.summary: Small branding images are delivered as legacy PNGs without responsive alternatives, including one oversized source.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all three images were PNG, none used srcset, and the 180x180 favicon source was displayed at 26x26. Lighthouse estimated 29 KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Export appropriately sized WebP/AVIF variants and use srcset/sizes where the rendered logo size varies; provide a true 26px favicon asset.

taskList.title: Make the advertised entertainment search/catalog journey real, or remove the claims and looping CTAs
Replace the repetitive keyword landing page with concise, content-first navigation
Deploy CSP and HSTS while retaining existing browser policies
Respect reduced motion and modernize scroll/route motion progressively
Optimize branding assets and component-level responsiveness
Use bidirectional logical properties for multilingual readiness
